cells.tense: This ending has your hand on it and a clear head behind the hand.
cells.ask: Try this once: put the phone face down and sit still for ten minutes, nothing else. What you get back is that tomorrow's work starts from farther inside you, and you can feel how much steadier your hands are.
cells.core:
You are clearing something out and you are level while you do it. Part of the ending is already decided and you are not dragging it behind you. You tidy up what is done, you tell people what changed, and you do not force the pace of it. When the next thing asks more than you thought you had, something in you holds, and you can feel the hold without putting a name on it.

The quiet has not arrived yet, and the ask is to make it: one short stretch lying still on purpose, no phone, no sorting through anything. It is small, and it keeps the part of the mind that has been running the ending from running you too.
cells.sheetLine: The ending is moving, and you are holding its pace.
cells.verb: letting the mind go quiet on purpose
cells.place: at an ending that is already underway

cells.tense: Your mind is already standing past the clearing, writing the chapter that has not opened yet.
cells.ask: Try this once: write the thing that is ending on a sheet of paper, read it out loud once, and put the sheet in a drawer. What you get back is that tomorrow's work starts under your feet instead of in front of them, and you can feel the difference in your body.
cells.core:
When this part of you is steady, you let the ending be what it is. You say what is done, you make room, and you do not rehearse the new chapter standing up. Your direction sits at your back and you move from there. That is a known place for you, and it is still in reach.

The mind will not settle because it is already defending a future you cannot write yet — the marker is out over a page that does not exist. The ask is one thing you would actually defend. Say it plainly, then stop. That is not settling the ending; it is giving your effort one direction to stand behind.
cells.sheetLine: You are bracing for a future with no line in it yet.
cells.verb: letting the mind go quiet on purpose

cells.tense: The door behind you is still open in how you live, so the ending has not been able to finish anything.
cells.ask: Try this once: send one short message to a person you are not finished with — something honest, two sentences, no request in it. What you get back is a pair of hands better set on the present, and you can feel the difference the moment it lands.
cells.core:
This part of you knows how to let a thing go, and when it works, you go one layer at a time. You clear what you can carry, you sleep through the night, and you let the cleared ground stay clear before you fill it. You recognize what genuinely pulls you and you do not confuse it with the need to have answered everything.

What is absent here is the quiet, and the recognition, not the effort. You keep the moment of deciding rehearsed in your head, so nothing gets to be real and your feeling stays rehearsed too. The ask is a small honest contact with one other person — not a resolution, just the truth of what is still unfinished in your own voice.

cells.tense: You are resting the mind and calling it the room's, but the room was built by you.
cells.ask: Try this once: name one thing you keep because it carries a person or a time — say out loud what it carried — then give it a place, keep it or pass it on, and say which. What you get back is a little more of your own story in your hands, and the room to choose what gets kept.
cells.core:
You are the one who stays level when a chapter closes. You are the one who tells the others what is next and how the week changes. You sort what stays, you hand back what does not belong to you, and you keep the place calm while it happens. That is a real gift, and people around you feel it as a floor under their feet.

That calm is yours — the call to let something be finished is coming from you — but you are describing it as something the place requires, as if the quiet were the house's and not yours. The ask is that you say one kept thing is yours to keep or pass on, out loud, once. The call was made; this is the owning of it.

attempts.check: Two unsupported things in the drafts: any claim that the person has been avoiding a particular ending, and any claim about what rest is currently getting them. The record gives a capacity (mind settling through calibration) in a seat of endings; it does not say what was ended, how long, or who was there. A reader could reasonably say 'I am resting plenty, I am not avoiding anything' — so the ask must be something like lying still on purpose and clearing one kept thing, which is useful whether or not the avoidance read is true. The sentence 'you are steering without knowing it' serves the writer more than the reader; it is cut, and the scene is kept to what a camera could see.
